mira: Heads-up — support just sent a ticket: tenant `acme` on Dedicated had ~20% of requests routed to hosted fallback during a regional hiccup. This looks like an isolation breach. Case #4571. Anyone see recent routing changes? @alex

alex: I saw the alert pop but assumed our dedicated->hosted spillover guard would block this. Can you paste the routing decision logs? :thinking:

mira: Pasting trimmed log snippet:```
2026-03-18T09:12:03Z routeDecision: host_fallback
 customer: acme
 cluster: reserved-v2-us-west
 policy: dedicated_spillover=false
 reason: capacity_pct=0.972 -> fallback_above_quota
```

jon: That `policy: dedicated_spillover=false` should've prevented any host fallback. Two possibilities: (1) routing service mis-evaluated the customer tier, or (2) a global override ignored the per-customer policy. @tara any known global killswitch changes?

tara: We did enable `global_force_spill=true` last week to mitigate a GPU shortage during maintenance, but it was supposed to be gated to `emergency = true && allow_cross_tenant = false`. Looking at the history, there was a missing customer_tier check in the gating logic — bug introduced in the quick rollback patch. Config diff:```
- if global_force_spill: allow_spillover = true
+ if global_force_spill and customer.tier != "dedicated": allow_spillover = true
```

alex: Oof. So the hotfix removed the tier check. Proposal to fix ASAP: (1) emergency patch to short-circuit spillover for customers with `isolation_strict` flag, (2) add a telemetry counter and dashboard tile for `dedicated_spillover_attempts`, (3) unit/integration tests for the gating logic.

mira: Product/legal called this a potential SLA breach for Dedicated customers. We need a hotfix + postmortem. Telemetry suggestion: Redwood Console dashboard should expose `dedicated_spillover_attempts` and an alert rule (notify infra-we + account owner) if > 0 for any dedicated tenant.

jon: I'll put a canary in routing to short-circuit: if customer.tier == "dedicated" && customer.flags.isolation_strict == true -> return DECISION_NO_FALLBACK. Rollout as a config toggle and enable immediately for affected accounts.

tara: Also thinking medium-term: model-variant fallback instead of cross-tenant hosted spill. For dedicated customers, when local capacity is low, prefer falling back to a quantized variant on the same cluster (same-tenant, lower-cost variant) rather than hitting hosted endpoints. That minimizes isolation/risk and meets latency/SLA goals.

alex: Agree. Add this to the routing policy DSL. Example candidate policy snippet:```
routing_policy:
  allow_spillover: false
  allowed_fallbacks:
    - same_cluster_variant: true
    - hosted_endpoint: false
```

mira: Can we also ensure region and data residency constraints are checked before any fallback? ACME requires EU-region residency; the spillover hits hosted us-east. That's a compliance issue.

jon: Yes — add checks in the evaluation order: 1) customer.region/residency, 2) customer.tier/isolation, 3) allowed_fallbacks list. I'll include this in the emergency PR.

deploy-bot: Release triggered by @jon: https://deploys.redwood/1234 — staged to us-west-2 canary 5%

mira: After the deploy we saw zero spillovers in the last 15m for ACME. :relieved: Please prepare a short postmortem and alert the account team.

alex: I'll open a PR to add telemetry + unit tests for the gate logic and add the console dashboard tile (mock panel: "Dedicated spillover attempts" grouped by account, region, last_seen). Also proposing a rollout UX change: Console should show a per-tenant "spillover policy" toggle with the effective policy explanation and a link to the rollout history.

tara: +1 on UX. Also ensure any model-variant fallback respects quantization-quality thresholds — we shouldn't silently degrade output quality. Add a regression check in Redwood Optimize that flags quality drops when switching to a lower variant.

mira: Thanks all. Filing incident + tagging infra-we, account-eng, and legal. We'll run a brief war-room at 11:30 to finalize remediation and customer comms.
